title: Per-session deviation stack and resume focus
summary: Per-caller focus and LIFO return stacks with atomic ownership and explicit restart recovery
description:
Implemented per-session isolation in T455-T457: WorkDeviation.ownerSession, deviationsForSession, per-session resume entries in .planner/.local/resume-sessions.json (20 recent callers), caller-aware selection/recap and MCP/Pi lifecycle paths. Sessionless callers retain the project-wide view; the guard bypass remains project-wide. Sources: packages/plan-core/src/session-focus.ts:1, packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:1913, packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts:256, packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:20, packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:67.

T458 is the follow-up for four failures found when heca-pro P010(F003)/T031 tested published 0.4.7: missing persisted MCP focus, false-positive foreign-owner starts, both concurrent callers reporting success and restart retaining an old owner while hiding active work. The implementation, committed as cf131dc and integrated into develop through PR #77, centralizes ownership in PlanStore.claimTask and explicit recovery in registerSession/recoverSessionForTask. MCP/Pi refresh caller focus on load/lifecycle and expose planner-session-recover/session_recover. Recovery uses an active or pending-return task reference, explicit confirmation, known-process liveness checks and a fresh destination caller; it transfers the complete return stack, owned work and notes without changing statuses or checkpoints. The canonical phase decision records the contract. Older owners without process records rely on explicit confirmation that the old caller has stopped.

Focused core, real stdio MCP and Pi regressions pass, including contention, idempotency, foreign-owner start/switch refusal, nested return recovery, legacy pending returns and rollback on write failure. T458 is completed locally. Canonical pnpm verify:final passed all seven steps for fingerprint 51e94d842c96, including 910/910 Node tests, browser end-to-end and freshly packed installed ownership/focus/nested-recovery smoke. A newly published-package recheck remains a separately approved release action; no npm publication is performed by this task.

Preserve per-caller LIFO/RESUME REQUIRED, recommendation/on-hold claims, pause history, original startedAt, context/guideline read gates, independent callers, sessionless read APIs and hidden internal caller IDs. No assignment/role policy is added to the planner.

Delivery update 2026-10-15: release preparation targets release/v0.4.8 (all five npm packages 0.4.8, plugins 0.3.8) through the canonical release script. Feature PR #77 CI passed. The release PR to main is the publication boundary and remains subject to the user's next decision.

Release preparation completed: PR #78 (https://github.com/ovidius72/agent-planner/pull/78) targets main from release/v0.4.8. Release commit 821f4a7; canonical release gate passed all seven steps for fingerprint 45990b26665f. Publication awaits the release PR merge; downstream published-package verification remains with heca-pro T031.

acceptedDecisions.title: Explicit task-referenced recovery preserves session work after caller restart
acceptedDecisions.decision: Task starts claim ownership atomically and report success only for the owning caller. MCP/Pi expose an explicit confirmed session-recovery operation identified by an active or pending-return task. Recovery transfers the previous caller's complete ownership, deviation stack and focus without changing task statuses, checkpoint history or read attestations. Registered live local processes are refused, and a destination caller with owned work cannot recover another stack.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Published 0.4.7 verification exposed false-positive starts, concurrent claims and loss of caller focus across restart. A task reference avoids application-side owner-ID mappings and preserves per-caller LIFO returns while allowing explicit recovery.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Shared core claimTask/registerSession/recoverSessionForTask; MCP planner-session-recover and Pi session_recover. Local process evidence is kept under .planner/.local/sessions. Legacy owners without records require explicit confirmation that the caller has stopped; a remote process whose exit cannot be verified is refused. Sessionless read APIs remain project-wide and expose no internal connection IDs.

tasks.title: Core: per-session deviation ownership and per-session resume focus
tasks.description:
Today every session of one planner shares two things. (1) The approved side-task stack: WorkDeviation (packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts:~108) records recommended/temporary/resume task ids but not WHO made the switch; the list lives in .planner/.local/deviations.json (plan-store.ts:1435 loadWorkDeviations, :2634 addWorkDeviation, :2641 setWorkDeviationState), so when agent A switches to a temporary task the return target is recorded for agent B as well. (2) The resume focus: one ResumeFocus (schema.ts:44) in .local/resume.json (plan-store.ts:1872 loadResume, :1881 saveResume, :1964 refreshResume), with inProgressTaskIds taken from EVERY in-progress task and one set of nextSteps/notes/lastSessionSummary. Task ownership is already per session (Task.activeOwnerSession, task-selection.ts:263). Work: add `ownerSession` (string, default "") to WorkDeviationSchema; new pure helper `deviationsForSession(deviations, sessionId)` in a plan-core module: empty sessionId returns all (today's behaviour), a session id returns its own plus unowned legacy ones; addWorkDeviation stamps the caller's session. Resume: keep resume.json as the project-level default (guardBypassUntil stays project-wide, it is not focus) and add per-session focus entries in .local/resume-sessions.json keyed by session id, bounded (keep the 20 most recently updated); loadResume/saveResume/refreshResume take an optional sessionId; a session's inProgressTaskIds are the tasks it owns (activeOwnerSession === sessionId). Sessionless callers get today's results exactly. No data migration needed (new fields default). Unit tests in packages/plan-core/test: helper filtering (own, other, legacy, sessionless), stamping on add, per-session resume isolation and pruning, sessionless unchanged.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped the core of per-session focus in plan-core. schema.ts: WorkDeviationSchema gains ownerSession (default "", so old stored data reads as unowned); ResumeSessionsSchema (record of session id to ResumeFocus). New packages/plan-core/src/session-focus.ts (exported from index.ts): deviationsForSession(deviations, sessionId) (own + unowned legacy visible, other sessions hidden, empty session id returns everything), pruneResumeSessions and RESUME_SESSION_LIMIT (20, most recently updated kept). plan-store.ts: addWorkDeviation(deviation, sessionId?) stamps the session unless the deviation already has an owner; loadResume/saveResume/refreshResume take an optional sessionId; per-session entries live in .planner/.local/resume-sessions.json (exclusive-create then atomicUpdateJson under the write lock, so concurrent sessions do not lose entries; pruned to the limit); a session with no entry yet inherits the project-level focus for READING; a session's inProgressTaskIds/currentPhaseId come only from tasks it owns (activeOwnerSession); guardBypassUntil stays project-level (never copied into a session entry; authorizeGuardBypass/isGuardBypassed untouched). Sessionless callers get exactly the previous results. Verified: packages/plan-core/test/session-focus.test.mjs, 15 tests (filtering, stamping, isolation, inheritance, ownership, bypass untouched, sessionless unchanged, concurrent saves, pruning); full plan-core suite 500/500 pass; builds. NOT done here (next task T456): nothing calls these with a session id yet, so behaviour in MCP/Pi/server is unchanged until T456/T457; recommendNextTask and recap still read all deviations. Not verified: full repository gate (phase close).

tasks.title: Use the caller's session in selection, switch, recap, MCP and server
tasks.description:
Builds on the core task (ownerSession + deviationsForSession + per-session resume). Every place that reads or writes deviations or resume focus must pass the caller's session so one agent's side task never becomes another agent's return target. Core: recommendNextTask/recommendNextWork (task-selection.ts:256-263, :362) and recap (recap.ts:66 pendingDeviation from plan.project.workDeviations, :247 recommendNextTask) filter with deviationsForSession; the load recap and planner-show use the session's own resume focus. MCP (packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts): task_switch, task_deviation, task_complete (RESUME REQUIRED), task_start and task_recommend pass plannerSessionId (index.ts:17-26) and stamp new deviations with it; recap/planner-load/planner-show pass it. Server (packages/plan-server/src/serve.ts, 9 call sites of loadResume/saveResume/workDeviations): the web UI is sessionless and keeps project-wide behaviour; the /api/v1 and entity events are unchanged. LIFO return semantics per session, the RESUME REQUIRED notice, on-hold claims and recommendation claims must behave exactly as today for a single session. Tests: packages/plan-core and packages/plan-mcp (MCP through a real client where the existing MCP tests do), covering: two sessions switch and return independently; session B's recommendation does not show A's RESUME REQUIRED; a sessionless web UI call still sees all.

---
**Completion summary:**
Made selection, recap and the MCP use the caller's session. plan-core: PlanStore.loadProject(sessionId?) returns only that session's (plus unowned) workDeviations; recommendNextTask filters deviations by session itself AND hides tasks another session set aside (a live deviation owned by another session points back at them) from both the checkpoint fallback and priority selection, so session B is never sent to, or forced to resume, session A's preserved task; addWorkDeviation accepts a deviation without ownerSession and stamps the session; buildRecap takes RecapOptions.sessionId (own resume focus, own pending deviation, session-aware next step). plan-mcp: task show/update/pause/switch/start/complete read loadProject(plannerSessionId); recommend/deviation/switch/start pass plannerSessionId to recommendNextTask/recommendNextWork with ALL deviations (new allWorkDeviations helper) because the selector does the hiding; switch and deviation stamp new deviations with the session; load recap passes the session. Server: unchanged on purpose, the web UI is sessionless and keeps project-wide behaviour. Found by the test: filtering the list before selection hid other sessions' checkpoints so B was still told to resume A's task; fixed in the selector. Verified: packages/plan-mcp/test/mcp-sessions.test.mjs (3 tests through real MCP servers: A returns, B not forced, single agent unchanged), plan-core session-focus tests 18/18 incl. selector cases, all 99 plan-mcp tests, all 500 plan-core tests, all 85 plan-server tests pass. Not verified: Pi adapter (next task T457), full repository gate (phase close). Known limit: a task that no live deviation points at but has a checkpoint is still offered to every session (shared checkpoint rule).

tasks.title: Pi adapter per-session focus, cross-adapter proof and docs
tasks.description:
Builds on the two previous tasks. The Pi adapter (packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts, 30 call sites of loadResume/saveResume/refreshResume/addWorkDeviation/setWorkDeviationState) has its own session ids (pi:...); pass them wherever the MCP now passes plannerSessionId so Pi and MCP agents on one planner each get their own side-task stack and resume focus. Add a parity test in the shared cross-harness matrix (see requirement Cross-harness semantic parity and the scenario helpers under test/) showing the same two-session scenario gives equivalent normalized outcomes through MCP and Pi. Document the behaviour: README.md (planner concepts) and the operating guide source (packages/plan-core/src/planner-skill.ts and .planner/SKILL.md managed copy if the canonical text changes; follow the managed-copy policy), stating that focus is per session, sessionless callers see project-wide state, and how heca-pro agents get isolation. Check that docs/api-v1.md needs no change (read API exposes no focus). Run the full gate once at the end of the phase.

---
**Completion summary:**
Pi adapter now uses per-session focus and the phase is verified. packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts: every loadResume/refreshResume/loadProject lookup, addWorkDeviation, recommendNextTask/recommendNextWork and buildRecap call passes the Pi session id; the repeated expression `pi:${ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()}` (9 places) now goes through one helper piSessionIdOf(ctx) and the recommend/deviation/pause/complete handlers derive the id from ctx instead of relying on the module-level variable. Centralization fix from the gate: the 'allWorkDeviations' helper existed in both mcp and pi (repo invariant: no function declared in more than one of mcp, pi-adapter, plan-server); replaced by PlanStore.listAllWorkDeviations() in plan-core used by both. Tests: packages/pi-adapter/test/pi-sessions.test.mjs (Pi: A's detour stamped pi:session-A, A told to return, session B not told nor offered T002, sessionless reader sees it); mirrors packages/plan-mcp/test/mcp-sessions.test.mjs. DEVIATION from the task text: the shared scenario matrix (test/scenario-matrix.mjs) was NOT extended; it has no switch scenarios at all and adding them needs runner step mappings per harness, so parity is pinned by the two mirrored adapter tests, the same way task-start-phase-order is. Docs: README.md section 'Several agents on one planner' (per-session tasks, side tasks, resume focus, sessionless view, legacy data, shared checkpoint rule); the canonical operating guide (planner-skill.ts / .planner/SKILL.md) was NOT changed to avoid a managed-copy and plugin-sync change; docs/api-v1.md needs no change (read API exposes no focus). Verified: full gate passed (build, typecheck, coverage, plugin sync, capability audit, browser e2e, packed install smoke) after one fix round; plan-core 503, plan-mcp 99, pi-adapter 97, plan-server 85 tests pass. Not verified: two real Pi and MCP sessions at the same time in one process (Pi keeps module state, so the Pi test runs sessions one after the other).

tasks.title: Fix atomic task ownership, persisted caller focus and restart recovery
tasks.description:
Follow-up to T455-T457 after heca-pro P010(F003)/T031 verified published agent-plan 0.4.7 and found four failures. Evidence: /Users/antonio/projects/heca-pro-planner-api/docs/planner-api-verification.md and scripts/planner-api-check/check.mjs. Existing session filtering and deviation stacks pass; the gaps are lifecycle ownership and persisted focus.

Current implementation: packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:2330 returns started=true for any already-in-progress task without checking activeOwnerSession; :2409-2455 writes ownership after out-of-lock eligibility reads and only verifies status. Switch has analogous writes at :2163. PlanStore.resumeTask (packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:3529) and updatePhase offer atomic file updates but no shared ownership-claim operation. PlanStore.loadResume/saveResume/refreshResume (:1913-2030) support per-session focus, but MCP load/lifecycle does not refresh it. stdio MCP session IDs are process-local (index.ts:20-26), so restarting changes the caller and leaves old ownership/return stacks.

Work: reproduce the reported cases using isolated mkdtemp fixtures and real stdio clients; centralize the ownership check and claim under core write coordination so one concurrent caller succeeds; make repeated starts honest and idempotent only for the owner; persist each caller's focus on load and successful lifecycle operations; expose supported explicit restart recovery that safely transfers the previous session's owned work, resume focus and complete LIFO deviation stack without erasing checkpoints or touching another caller. Document recovery semantics and test active detours and pending nested returns. Keep ownership logic harness-agnostic and use it in the Pi lifecycle paths where applicable.

Preserve independent tasks for different callers, sessionless project-wide reads, legacy data compatibility, original startedAt/completion evidence, checkpoints/pause history, per-caller LIFO/RESUME REQUIRED semantics, Project Guidelines/context gates, read-only /api/v1 and its hidden internal IDs, and existing Web UI contracts. Do not edit another real project's planner, invent client-side owner-ID mappings, or automatically steal live ownership.

Verification: use scripts/verify.mjs for focused affected targets, then the canonical final gate once before closeout. Exercise freshly packed installed artifacts with real MCP clients and the four external regression cases; a published-package recheck remains a later release validation requiring explicit release approval. No commit, push, PR or publish is authorized by this task.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented and verified the four ownership/focus failures reported by heca-pro P010(F003)/T031 for published agent-plan 0.4.7. Working branch: wip/planner-session-ownership, based on synchronized develop 2b74ead. Changes remain uncommitted for review.

Core: packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts:3502 claimTask serializes canonical ownership checks and writes under the root lock, refuses foreign active/return-stack ownership, preserves original startedAt and gives idempotent success only to the owner. recoverSessionForTask (:3541) requires explicit confirmation, identifies the old session by an active/pending-return task, refuses registered live processes/remote unverifiable owners/occupied destination callers, transfers all owned work and the complete deviation stack/focus, preserves task status/checkpoint/pause history and rolls back on write failures with persistence read-back. Local process registration lives under .planner/.local/sessions. packages/plan-core/src/session-focus.ts centralizes ownership including paused return reservations; task-start-outcome.ts includes TASK_OWNED_BY_ANOTHER_SESSION.

MCP/Pi use the shared claim for task starts and switches, verify persisted ownership, refresh caller focus on load/successful lifecycle operations, and expose planner-session-recover/session_recover. Load preparation retains typed failure diagnostics; web server creation stays outside transaction async context. Context/guideline gates and sessionless read-only /api/v1 contracts remain intact. Tests added/updated in core session-focus, MCP mcp-sessions/mcp-harness and Pi pi-sessions/host-registration. README, canonical planner skill and all generated plugin skill mirrors document supported recovery; test surface/scenario inventories include the operations. scripts/installed-artifact-smoke.mjs now exercises ownership, contention, focus and nested recovery using freshly packed packages in a mkdtemp installation.

Verification on 2026-10-14: the four real stdio regressions first failed against the prior implementation and now pass. Focused core/MCP/Pi regressions and affected inventory/load diagnostic tests pass. The first final gate exposed three test/diagnostic defects, corrected with focused verification. The final pnpm verify:final passed all seven steps for fingerprint 51e94d842c96: build, typecheck, coverage (910/910 Node tests, zero skipped/failed), plugin synchronization, capability audit, browser end-to-end and freshly packed installation smoke. Evidence: .planner/.local/verification/final-gate.json and 51e94d842c96-*.log. git diff --check passes. The packed smoke verifies two nested LIFO returns and an independent caller, plus exactly one successful concurrent owner. Full gate must be reused while the source fingerprint is unchanged.

Phase decision 5a7e9fce-0750-4b20-af65-114cff063d7d defines explicit task-referenced recovery. Limit: legacy owners without process records rely on explicit confirmation that the old caller has stopped. No global install, commit, push, PR or npm publication was performed. Rechecking a newly published version in heca-pro remains a later release/downstream validation; no change was made to that project's planner.
